tour.name: Petra Private Day Trip from Amman: the Siq, the Treasury, the Royal Tombs & the Monastery
tour.subtitle: The rose-red city of the Nabataeans in one private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the narrow Siq gorge, the first sight of the Treasury, the Street of Facades, the theatre and Royal Tombs, the colonnaded street and, for the energetic, the climb to the Monastery.

tour.overview:
Petra was the capital of the Nabataeans, Arab traders who grew rich on the incense and spice routes and carved their tombs and temples into the pink sandstone cliffs of southern Jordan from around the 1st century BC. Forgotten by the West for centuries and revealed to Europe by the Swiss explorer Johann Ludwig Burckhardt in 1812, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985 and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World since 2007.

This private day trip takes you from Amman to Petra and back with a licensed guide and a vehicle, about three hours each way on the Desert Highway, with a full day in the ancient city.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 14 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Amman or at the Dead Sea
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; licensed Petra guide on site
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; 8 to 15 kilometres of walking

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Siq and the Treasury.
• The Street of Facades and the theatre.
• The Royal Tombs.
• The colonnaded street and the Great Temple.
• The Monastery (optional climb).

WHY THIS WORKS
A private vehicle lets you leave early and reach the Treasury before the crowds; your guide sets the pace of the walking.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, walkers, families and photographers with only one day.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To see Petra by Night and more of the site, choose our Petra and Wadi Rum 2-day tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Petra involves a lot of walking on uneven ground. Bring sun protection; there is little shade. If you hold the Jordan Pass, Petra entry is included in it.

days.name: The Siq, the Treasury, the Royal Tombs and the Monastery
days.description:
What to expect: the Nabataean city of Petra, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrance and lunch.

Your driver collects you at about 6:00 and drives south on the Desert Highway, about 3 hours, to Wadi Musa, the town at the gate of Petra, where your licensed guide meets you.

You walk down the Siq, a narrow cleft between cliffs up to 80 metres high, with traces of the Nabataean water channels and carved niches, until the gorge opens and the Treasury appears, its 40-metre facade glowing pink in the morning light. Your guide explains its Hellenistic architecture and the legends of the treasure said to be hidden in its urn. You continue along the Street of Facades, past the 4,000-seat theatre carved into the rock, to the Royal Tombs – the Urn, Silk, Corinthian and Palace tombs – with their swirling bands of coloured sandstone.

After lunch in the city centre, near the colonnaded street and the Great Temple, the energetic can climb some 800 rock-cut steps to the Monastery, Ad Deir, an even larger facade on a mountaintop, with views towards Wadi Araba; others can explore the Great Temple and Qasr al-Bint. You walk back through the Siq in the afternoon light and drive back to Amman.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:00 – Pick-up in Amman.
09:15 – Arrival in Petra.
09:30 – The Siq and the Treasury.
11:00 – Street of Facades, theatre and Royal Tombs.
12:30 – Colonnaded street and lunch.
13:30 – Climb to the Monastery (optional).
16:00 – Walk back through the Siq.
17:00 – Drive back.
20:00 – Back in Amman.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Donkeys are offered for the Monastery climb; we recommend walking, for the animals’ welfare.
• Little Petra can be added on the way out.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed Petra guide, entrance ticket, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: horse or carriage rides, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: About 8 kilometres to the city centre and back, or 15 with the Monastery climb.

faq.question: Is the entrance ticket included?
faq.answer: Yes. If you have the Jordan Pass, which includes Petra, we deduct it.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at a restaurant in Petra.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who can walk; the Siq is downhill on the way in and uphill on the way back.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Electric carts can be booked for the Siq for those with limited mobility.

faq.question: Can we see Petra by Night?
faq.answer: Yes, on our 2-day tour; it runs on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings.

faq.question: Is Jordan safe?
faq.answer: Jordan is one of the safest and most welcoming countries in the region.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable walking shoes, a hat, sun protection and modest clothing; layers in winter.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
